# Zydis provenance

## Source

- Repository: `https://github.com/zyantific/zydis.git`, vendored as the git
  submodule `zydis.submodule`.
- Pinned tag: `v4.1.1`
- Pinned commit: `a2278f1d254e492f6a6b39f6cb5d1f5d515659dc`
- Nested submodule (Zydis's own dependency): `dependencies/zycore` ->
  `https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c`, commit
  `0b2432ced0884fd152b471d97ecf0258ff4d859f`.
- License: MIT (`LICENSE` in this folder, copied verbatim from the submodule
  for redistribution alongside the built DLL).

## Runtime version quirk (verified against source, not guessed)

`ZydisGetVersion()` returns the literal `ZYDIS_VERSION` macro
(`include/Zydis/Zydis.h`), which at commit `a2278f1d2` is hardcoded to
`0x0004000100000000` — major 4, minor 1, **patch 0**, build 0 — even though
the CMake project version (`CMakeLists.txt`, `project(Zydis VERSION 4.1.1.0 ...)`)
and the git tag both say `4.1.1`. The macro was not bumped for the 4.1.1 patch
release. `ZydisApi.pas`'s load-time version check must therefore compare
major/minor (`>= 4.1`), never expect an exact `4.1.1.0` match against
`ZydisGetVersion()` — an exact-match check would reject this exact DLL.

## Build environment

- Visual Studio 2026 Community, MSVC toolset `14.51.36231`
  (`cl.exe` reports `19.51.36248.0`).
- CMake: the copy bundled with Visual Studio,
  `Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\CMake\CMake\bin\cmake.exe`.
- Generator: `NMake Makefiles` (avoids depending on Ninja being on `PATH`;
  both `cl` and `nmake` come from `VsDevCmd.bat`).
- Built: 2026-08-08.

## Exact invocation

```bat
call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\Tools\VsDevCmd.bat" -arch=x64 -host_arch=x64

cmake -G "NMake Makefiles" ^
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_SHARED_LIB=ON ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_TESTS=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_MAN=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_BUILD_DOXYGEN=OFF ^
  -DZYDIS_FEATURE_ENCODER=ON ^
  ..\zydis.submodule

cmake --build . --config Release
```

`ZYDIS_FEATURE_ENCODER=ON` is Zydis's default; it is listed explicitly because
the encoder is not currently used by `ZydisApi.pas` but costs nothing to keep
available for a later increment (e.g. NOP-filling a patched region).

This is exactly what `build_zydis.bat` in this folder runs (`cd /d %~dp0`,
resolve `VsDevCmd.bat` and `cmake.exe` by their absolute install paths, clean
`build\`, configure, build, copy `build\Zydis.dll` to `bin\x64\Zydis.dll`,
hash it). It is **not** called by `build_all.bat`, `build_dap.bat` or
`build_debug.bat` — those stay Delphi-only. Run it by hand, from the repo, any
time the pinned submodule commit changes:

```bat
git submodule update --init --recursive ThirdParty\Zydis\zydis.submodule
call ThirdParty\Zydis\build_zydis.bat
```

## Output

- `bin\x64\Zydis.dll` — 576,512 bytes.
- SHA-256: `f81ca7d636d4679a0794da84dc32790d270b9c9bf293722844cd3ac4302ea745`
  (also in `bin\x64\Zydis.dll.sha256`, regenerated by the build script via
  `certutil -hashfile ... SHA256`).
- One x64 DLL. The machine mode (32-bit vs 64-bit target code) is a decoder
  parameter passed at call time (`ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LEGACY_32` /
  `ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LONG_64`), not a build variant — verified by
  `DevTools\DisasmProbe.exe`, which decodes real bytes from both a 32-bit and
  a 64-bit `TestTarget.exe` through this one DLL.
- Exports verified with `dumpbin /exports` (43 total): `ZydisDisassembleIntel`,
  `ZydisGetVersion` and `ZydisIsFeatureEnabled` are present, matching what
  `ZydisApi.pas` imports.
- Runtime dependencies verified with `dumpbin /dependents`: `KERNEL32.dll`,
  `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, `api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll`,
  `api-ms-win-crt-string-l1-1-0.dll`. The last three are the dynamic MSVC / UCRT
  runtime (default CMake `/MD` build) — present on any machine with the VC++
  redistributable or a recent Windows 10/11 install, but not guaranteed on a
  bare machine. Static-linking the CRT (`/MT`, `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY`) to
  drop this dependency is a candidate for the packaging increment, not done
  here.

## Verification questions answered (DISASSEMBLY_PLAN.md, increment 1)

1. **Version and API shape** — `ZydisDisassembleIntel` exists exactly as the
   plan assumed (`include/Zydis/Disassembler.h`), confirmed by both source
   inspection and the exports table above. See the version-quirk note above
   for the one surprise (`ZydisGetVersion()` under-reports the patch digit).
2. **Maintained Pascal bindings** — `zyantific/zydis-pascal` exists and is
   listed as an official Zydis binding (MIT). It is a full header translation
   (static AND dynamic linkage, `TZydisDecoder`/`TZydisFormatter` classes, the
   whole API surface), last updated 2023-11-20 — it predates this pinned
   `v4.1.1` tag (2025-02-16) and was not re-verified against it. Using it would
   also contradict the plan's already-decided design (minimal explicit-import
   surface, dynamic `LoadLibrary` with an app-owned version gate, only the two
   entry points actually used). Not adopted; `ZydisApi.pas` is hand-written.
3. **One DLL, both machine modes** — confirmed by the CMake option
   `ZYDIS_BUILD_SHARED_LIB` (no per-architecture build knob in Zydis's own
   CMakeLists) and empirically by `DisasmProbe.exe` decoding both a 32-bit and
   a 64-bit target through the single built DLL.
